question: Can a person qualify for the federal Non-Insured Health Benefits program as an Inuit client even if they aren’t registered under the Indian Act?
generated_answer: You may qualify for the Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB) Program as an Inuit client, even if you are not registered under the Indian Act. You must be recognized as an Inuk by your Inuit community. You must also meet the NIHB eligibility criteria. You can apply for NIHB coverage by completing the online application form. You will need to provide proof of your Inuit status, such as a letter from your Inuit community or a copy of your Inuit birth certificate. Once you have submitted your application, it will be reviewed to determine if you are eligible for NIHB coverage. If you are eligible, you will be covered for the services listed in the NIHB Program. If you are not eligible, you will be notified of the reasons for the denial. You can also apply for NIHB coverage through your Inuit community. Your Inuit community may have a NIHB application form that you can complete and submit to the NIHB Program. Your Inuit community may also have a NIHB liaison officer who can help you with the application process.
